transcript.text: Alright, let's get started. As we all know, the new event-ingestion service is scheduled to enter production next Monday. Before we finalize, I need to walk through the architecture sign-off checklist with each of you. I'll be asking backend engineering, infrastructure, customer success operations, and security for any blockers or required controls before I record the final design. The draft currently proposes active-active replication, a 90-day event-retention period, and an initial limit of 96 partitions. Who'd like to go first with their review status?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to raise a blocker before we finalize. While reviewing an unrelated consumer integration this morning, I confirmed that the existing Ledger event consumer cannot preserve ordering across active-active replication. Production compatibility requires active-passive replication plus an explicit per-aggregate ordering guardrail. I have not yet updated the architecture document, but this directly conflicts with the draft design's active-active replication proposal.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a blocker on the partition count. I confirmed from the current production load model just ten minutes ago that the shared cluster can only support at most 48 partitions for this service without starving the checkout stream — not the 96 in the draft. I was still reconciling the capacity worksheet and hadn't posted the number yet, but this needs to be factored in before we finalize.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a blocker from a customer-success contract review I conducted this afternoon. The enterprise tenant Linden requires all event processing and storage to remain in the EU region only. Linden is included in the proposed initial cohort, and I have not yet added the required EU-only routing exception to the design ticket. This conflicts with the draft design's active-active replication approach, which would replicate Linden's events across regions.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a security blocker. During a separate token-hardening task today, my security scan found personal data in the event payloads. This means the service requires field-level encryption and a maximum 30-day retention period — not the 90 days proposed in the draft. I have not yet opened the security finding, but this needs to be addressed before we go to production next Monday.
